records.toxicity_detail: Foliage only, not the ripe fruit. NC State lists the poison parts as leaves and stems, toxic principle the alkaloids tomatine and solanine, severity Medium, and tags the plant a problem for cats, dogs and horses. The ripe fruit is the ordinary edible crop and is not implicated. NC State also records that, according to a Carolinas Poison Center clinical toxicologist, since that database began in 1997 there has been only one reference to a child having a reaction related to consuming tomato leaves or stems. The realistic risk is therefore from large quantities of foliage, e.g. a browsing animal, rather than an incidental nibble.

records.name_note: The species is Cucumis melo L. NC State Extension treats 'flexuosus' not as a botanical variety but as a horticultural cultivar group within the species, listing 'Flexuosus group (American cucumber)' among the informal groupings of C. melo alongside Cantalupensis, Inodorus and others. The accepted name is therefore recorded as Cucumis melo, with 'var. flexuosus' / 'Flexuosus Group' treated as an infraspecific cultivar designation. POWO's ranking of the varietal name was not independently confirmed (the POWO page returned HTTP 403), so this reflects extension usage rather than a checked nomenclatural database entry. Note also that NC State labels the group 'American cucumber' while this record's common name says 'Armenian cucumber'; the two labels should not be conflated in UI copy.
